Do not return hashes; the host binds immutable hashes.", "context": {"title": "David Copperfield", "unit": 7, "heading": "CHAPTER 5. I AM SENT AWAY FROM HOME", "previous_rows": [{"source_id": "en85-u007-b0062", "target": "— Котлеты, — сказал я.", "source_sha256": "1d8d9fe70f6b10100c03fbb3b910070d5164768609836e6cb6056d050f06d48b", "target_id": "ru-en85-u007-b0062", "tag": "p", "target_sha256": "64cfc853c5ca217883140b400910351e7095ab418ff6c0ae191fd416aafd6f3a"}, {"source_id": "en85-u007-b0063", "target": "— Господи помилуй! — воскликнул он. — А я и не знал, что это котлеты. Да ведь котлета — это как раз то, что надо, чтобы снять дурное действие этого пива! Вот повезло, а?", "source_sha256": "4a2c551e53ee46ca609de3850c5513a844ff84babc6ecb53dce413ff0f6d8f9d", "target_id": "ru-en85-u007-b0063", "tag": "p", "target_sha256": "a8ea1aa2c118ebe32adbe7962b40ef86a8ad5ffc665294262dc319d81949eb5c"}], "source_language": "English", "part": null, "book": null, "chapter": 5, "role": "chapter"}, "source_rows": [{"id": "en85-u007-b0064", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "So he took a chop by the bone in one hand, and a potato in the other, and ate away with a very good appetite, to my extreme satisfaction. He afterwards took another chop, and another potato; and after that, another chop and another potato. When we had done, he brought me a pudding, and having set it before me, seemed to ruminate, and to become absent in his mind for some moments.", "sha256": "02cb175f0bdb1339b84ef866cb6478cde420c1a8c6e2a7c1ab3eaef384ba1e7b", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[12]/p[65]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u007-b0065", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘How’s the pie?’ he said, rousing himself.", "sha256": "15042599b46e07db46e86832e98e504e1c06ff57723a97b4544cfd414c76614f", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[12]/p[66]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u007-b0066", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘It’s a pudding,’ I made answer.", "sha256": "39c225c494152cf7df93842d2ffdc277cbee6bcb821f05b74e0cefb8d64e5026", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[12]/p[67]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u007-b0067", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Pudding!’ he exclaimed. ‘Why, bless me, so it is! What!’ looking at it nearer. ‘You don’t mean to say it’s a batter-pudding!’", "sha256": "92652a140f124dfa7eb676168ace3333214c39f27c5a2249caceff4ed52bd0a7", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[12]/p[68]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u007-b0068", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Yes, it is indeed.’", "sha256": "715f1992ec179ca5de342f31a79c1a3b5a3bf0f32cb771d8e8bc8d786b80dd11", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[12]/p[69]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u007-b0069", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Why, a batter-pudding,’ he said, taking up a table-spoon, ‘is my favourite pudding! Ain’t that lucky? Come on, little ‘un, and let’s see who’ll get most.’", "sha256": "f1be0a5b000c75c175fa4fd6810fb31583a23107cc647d1f4c2e4ca55ec15497", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[12]/p[70]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u007-b0070", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "The waiter certainly got most. He entreated me more than once to come in and win, but what with his table-spoon to my tea-spoon, his dispatch to my dispatch, and his appetite to my appetite, I was left far behind at the first mouthful, and had no chance with him. I never saw anyone enjoy a pudding so much, I think; and he laughed, when it was all gone, as if his enjoyment of it lasted still.", "sha256": "4bce23a096a25e1061e0945e61734e355c049d650f242b6db8009ec1597cfb21", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[12]/p[71]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u007-b0071", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Finding him so very friendly and companionable, it was then that I asked for the pen and ink and paper, to write to Peggotty. He not only brought it immediately, but was good enough to look over me while I wrote the letter. When I had finished it, he asked me where I was going to school.", "sha256": "1e49cf5a2a74cb715f084b4785eda0f11fc166c23af07deacfe31f5c2f3272b7", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[12]/p[72]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u007-b0072", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I said, ‘Near London,’ which was all I knew.", "sha256": "b75f6d66a037d682fee4e23337ef70b4b5f9eee3d3b4c99dd740aeb14c5c0c84", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[12]/p[73]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u007-b0073", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Oh! my eye!’ he said, looking very low-spirited, ‘I am sorry for that.’", "sha256": "f9b74f03f639f508e40019f43f3a00d2b7303beae67bb79d2c41bd15f7896eee", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[12]/p[74]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u007-b0074", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Why?’ I asked him.", "sha256": "63cc9985198466453a84cf2f4268134599934c394435a80aa727bd6ae73acd31", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[12]/p[75]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u007-b0075", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Oh, Lord!’ he said, shaking his head, ‘that’s the school where they broke the boy’s ribs—two ribs—a little boy he was. I should say he was—let me see—how old are you, about?’", "sha256": "542244f5bff7faf26f1b26d3815c50e1d94f00f38dfe9370530243ecf85d1c56", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[12]/p[76]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u007-b0076", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I told him between eight and nine.", "sha256": "ec2bede6da4eeb4f95e3dc9f821d91f4a486a9aa12a31c28a4385499ddf75168", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[12]/p[77]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u007-b0077", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘That’s just his age,’ he said. ‘He was eight years and six months old when they broke his first rib; eight years and eight months old when they broke his second, and did for him.’", "sha256": "857ae81e210429154fba52c80a680948c02e96b4d6cf83a8b14232c42f0ffae0", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[12]/p[78]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u007-b0078", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I could not disguise from myself, or from the waiter, that this was an uncomfortable coincidence, and inquired how it was done. His answer was not cheering to my spirits, for it consisted of two dismal words, ‘With whopping.’", "sha256": "c406dac7d1938199bbc3859f5f271fce5bbe0869f1d3e37555a81445cf8dac19", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[12]/p[79]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u007-b0079", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "The blowing of the coach-horn in the yard was a seasonable diversion, which made me get up and hesitatingly inquire, in the mingled pride and diffidence of having a purse (which I took out of my pocket), if there were anything to pay.", "sha256": "6db8e416732d48862ef4aaec62b5c7518c4cb6552f310ac5a807e9957fac0d02", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[12]/p[80]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u007-b0080", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘There’s a sheet of letter-paper,’ he returned. ‘Did you ever buy a sheet of letter-paper?’", "sha256": "c140af145decc56371ff9497d025df1fa9642be671759e1325b14d15e43eea63", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[12]/p[81]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u007-b0081", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I could not remember that I ever had.", "sha256": "c29205ef6e4344495a20d9b75f6618655272113cd77c7deb6b122af8f10c7ad8", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[12]/p[82]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u007-b0082", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘It’s dear,’ he said, ‘on account of the duty. Threepence. That’s the way we’re taxed in this country. There’s nothing else, except the waiter. Never mind the ink. I lose by that.’", "sha256": "221eafa6c263ffa025eab7907e29a2ef0513d636437249984c2c46d0b9f1679b", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[12]/p[83]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u007-b0083", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘What should you—what should I—how much ought I to—what would it be right to pay the waiter, if you please?’ I stammered, blushing.", "sha256": "c3afc738377e0ca1aa23c1d18644bca3db623758764c84d91a6adb8da2173d09", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[12]/p[84]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u007-b0084", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘If I hadn’t a family, and that family hadn’t the cowpock,’ said the waiter, ‘I wouldn’t take a sixpence. If I didn’t support a aged pairint, and a lovely sister,’—here the waiter was greatly agitated—‘I wouldn’t take a farthing. If I had a good place, and was treated well here, I should beg acceptance of a trifle, instead of taking of it. But I live on broken wittles—and I sleep on the coals’—here the waiter burst into tears.", "sha256": "4f82414005732f116c11898ed739a3768e2b1ca109f1a7893a129ada5a341d91", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[12]/p[85]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u007-b0085", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I was very much concerned for his misfortunes, and felt that any recognition short of ninepence would be mere brutality and hardness of heart. Therefore I gave him one of my three bright shillings, which he received with much humility and veneration, and spun up with his thumb, directly afterwards, to try the goodness of.", "sha256": "d652167fe7cf0adf6b5996ca0fb7f66fb597c1e5d612d697e917562bc708be8e", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[12]/p[86]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u007-b0086", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "It was a little disconcerting to me, to find, when I was being helped up behind the coach, that I was supposed to have eaten all the dinner without any assistance. I discovered this, from overhearing the lady in the bow-window say to the guard, ‘Take care of that child, George, or he’ll burst!’ and from observing that the women-servants who were about the place came out to look and giggle at me as a young phenomenon. My unfortunate friend the waiter, who had quite recovered his spirits, did not appear to be disturbed by this, but joined in the general admiration without being at all confused. If I had any doubt of him, I suppose this half awakened it; but I am inclined to believe that with the simple confidence of a child, and the natural reliance of a child upon superior years (qualities I am very sorry any children should prematurely change for worldly wisdom), I had no serious mistrust of him on the whole, even then.", "sha256": "197379d2f98d6947f0bf9936feff7aa9545920c4da7f9e50c5364d25cb8df15b", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[12]/p[87]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u007-b0087", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I felt it rather hard, I must own, to be made, without deserving it, the subject of jokes between the coachman and guard as to the coach drawing heavy behind, on account of my sitting there, and as to the greater expediency of my travelling by waggon. The story of my supposed appetite getting wind among the outside passengers, they were merry upon it likewise; and asked me whether I was going to be paid for, at school, as two brothers or three, and whether I was contracted for, or went upon the regular terms; with other pleasant questions. But the worst of it was, that I knew I should be ashamed to eat anything, when an opportunity offered, and that, after a rather light dinner, I should remain hungry all night—for I had left my cakes behind, at the hotel, in my hurry. My apprehensions were realized. When we stopped for supper I couldn’t muster courage to take any, though I should have liked it very much, but sat by the fire and said I didn’t want anything. This did not save me from more jokes, either; for a husky-voiced gentleman with a rough face, who had been eating out of a sandwich-box nearly all the way, except when he had been drinking out of a bottle, said I was like a boa-constrictor who took enough at one meal to last him a long time; after which, he actually brought a rash out upon himself with boiled beef.", "sha256": "c3ce4a1152355eb124c5996625e25c0ac428f0eb598a1fe4ebedf2b371a76971", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[12]/p[88]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u007-b0088", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "We had started from Yarmouth at three o’clock in the afternoon, and we were due in London about eight next morning. It was Mid-summer weather, and the evening was very pleasant. When we passed through a village, I pictured to myself what the insides of the houses were like, and what the inhabitants were about; and when boys came running after us, and got up behind and swung there for a little way, I wondered whether their fathers were alive, and whether they were happy at home. I had plenty to think of, therefore, besides my mind running continually on the kind of place I was going to—which was an awful speculation. Sometimes, I remember, I resigned myself to thoughts of home and Peggotty; and to endeavouring, in a confused blind way, to recall how I had felt, and what sort of boy I used to be, before I bit Mr. Murdstone: which I couldn’t satisfy myself about by any means, I seemed to have bitten him in such a remote antiquity.", "sha256": "69d541e1bdb2930227f3e507f4e516a80d9d890a7aa80241fbecbd5506123acd", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[12]/p[89]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u007-b0089", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "The night was not so pleasant as the evening, for it got chilly; and being put between two gentlemen (the rough-faced one and another) to prevent my tumbling off the coach, I was nearly smothered by their falling asleep, and completely blocking me up. They squeezed me so hard sometimes, that I could not help crying out, ‘Oh! If you please!’—which they didn’t like at all, because it woke them. Opposite me was an elderly lady in a great fur cloak, who looked in the dark more like a haystack than a lady, she was wrapped up to such a degree. This lady had a basket with her, and she hadn’t known what to do with it, for a long time, until she found that on account of my legs being short, it could go underneath me. It cramped and hurt me so, that it made me perfectly miserable; but if I moved in the least, and made a glass that was in the basket rattle against something else (as it was sure to do), she gave me the cruellest poke with her foot, and said, ‘Come, don’t YOU fidget. YOUR bones are young enough, I’m sure!’", "sha256": "36f995356f90713fd198d3987638ac9a3cb9451ca058eda8302dcfd38bbfcece", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[12]/p[90]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u007-b0090", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "At last the sun rose, and then my companions seemed to sleep easier. The difficulties under which they had laboured all night, and which had found utterance in the most terrific gasps and snorts, are not to be conceived. As the sun got higher, their sleep became lighter, and so they gradually one by one awoke. I recollect being very much surprised by the feint everybody made, then, of not having been to sleep at all, and by the uncommon indignation with which everyone repelled the charge. I labour under the same kind of astonishment to this day, having invariably observed that of all human weaknesses, the one to which our common nature is the least disposed to confess (I cannot imagine why) is the weakness of having gone to sleep in a coach.", "sha256": "4fddac5e59a302b8939d4e8cb8ca022e8df52b2c25ce723a2b7e5ef6c6a42f56", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[12]/p[91]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u007-b0091", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "What an amazing place London was to me when I saw it in the distance, and how I believed all the adventures of all my favourite heroes to be constantly enacting and re-enacting there, and how I vaguely made it out in my own mind to be fuller of wonders and wickedness than all the cities of the earth, I need not stop here to relate. We approached it by degrees, and got, in due time, to the inn in the Whitechapel district, for which we were bound. I forget whether it was the Blue Bull, or the Blue Boar; but I know it was the Blue Something, and that its likeness was painted up on the back of the coach.", "sha256": "47bb6d03f0344a62a4720102213e9ab686bf373672321bd846736614a34fe8f8", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[12]/p[92]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u007-b0092", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "The guard’s eye lighted on me as he was getting down, and he said at the booking-office door:", "sha256": "611a94abe8bbbe35c9a4f81baa003d359c546bf2c8c3608e6112e248b79f866e", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[12]/p[93]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u007-b0093", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Is there anybody here for a yoongster booked in the name of Murdstone, from Bloonderstone, Sooffolk, to be left till called for?’", "sha256": "d9b0962092ae3f90dc8a7a8a7f30a1893373224a4812680abd5b3eb8c3e903e4", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[12]/p[94]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u007-b0094", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Nobody answered.", "sha256": "3969a2b6ae78e8af220a05bfd768f9e791ca82894a3f03e8a45c2e62ff81d596", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[12]/p[95]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u007-b0095", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Try Copperfield, if you please, sir,’ said I, looking helplessly down.", "sha256": "b91a19597bd5e1497c43c735bcc0703ac2cdeaf956b7c073dc51b2d02b602418", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[12]/p[96]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}]}
